Apply now The NSF I-Corps Hub: Desert and Pacific Region offers three types of regional I-Corps training opportunities. I-Corps Aspire A four-week virtual customer discovery course focused on problem validation and early market exploration. Teams conduct at least 15 customer discovery interviews across four Zoom sessions, unless otherwise specified by the host institution. I-Corps Immerse A five-week, fully funded customer discovery experience that combines virtual training with in-person conference attendance. Teams conduct 50 customer discovery interviews to validate markets and advance toward business-model fit. I-Corps Catalyze A five-session virtual course for startups pursuing SBIR funding or private capital. Teams conduct 20 customer discovery interviews to strengthen commercialization plans and pitch

There are multiple ways you can get involved: apply now for an upcoming training, join the team or sign up for our mailing list to stay informed. Apply now Meet Our Teaching Team Become An Instructor Contact Us Meet Our Teaching Team Become An Instructor Contact Us Meet our Teaching Team Our regional courses are led by a talented and diverse group of instructors from across the Desert and Pacific Region. These experts have extensive knowledge of the I-Corps methodology and employ proven strategies to guide teams through the customer discovery process, all while creating an inclusive and supportive learning atmosphere. Leith Martin Leith Martin Hub Co-Director, Hub Lead Instructor, Regional Instructor, and National Instructor Why am I an instructor? I love seeing teams change. What is exciting about participating in I-Corps? If you commit to the process you will be
The advantages to participating include, entrepreneurial education, networking, skill development and developing future funding opportunities.

It’s a wonderful way to support different teams (faculty, staff, students, community members, industry mentors) and their potential solutions, aiming to solve real-world problems with new products and services.
My interdisciplinary skill set helps me advise deep tech teams.
I started my career at a major aerospace company where I developed mathematical models of missile navigation systems.
My education and experience allow me to meet teams where they are and help them explore commercial opportunities.
I have spent 20 years in a role of medical device ideation and development, so I can offer some insight into the industry, the process of bringing a device to market, and contacts in the industry.
Helping graduate students and faculty realize that they are already well-equipped to do as much customer discovery work as they are interested in is so satisfying.

As a start-up founder, the National program taught me to center my company around the problems and experiences of my customers, rather than my shiny new technology toys, and helped me secure contracts with large aerospace companies.
Now, as a Regional Instructor, I strive to help folks also embarking on the deep-tech path focus on what value they provide and maximize their chance of success.

MORE Become an Instructor or Mentor In addition to our instructors, seasoned entrepreneurs act as mentors, providing invaluable support and insights as teams navigate the business ecosystem throughout their I-Corps journey.

Together, we’re transforming cutting-edge ideas into impactful products and services. What We Offer Program Information FAQs Hub Partners What We Offer Program Information FAQs Hub Partners What We Offer At the NSF I-Corps Hub: Desert and Pacific Region, we focus on five key activities to empower innovation: Recruiting We actively recruit teams from the Desert and Pacific Region to boost participation in Regional and National I-Corps, expanding opportunities for researchers and innovators. Training Attending our regional I-Corps training will boost your team’s chances for a $50,000 grant and prepare for National I-Corps. We also train instructors at the regional level to prepare for national instructional leadership
Support We assist higher education institutions in joining I-Corps, welcoming new partner institutions to expand our network and impact.
Stories of impact We promote the positive impact that university research makes in the world through the stories we tell about the faculty from our member universities who participate in I-Corps.
High-performing teams could also earn a spot in the National I-Corps Teams program, with potential grants of $50,000 to further develop their ventures through deeper customer discovery.
NSF I-Corps is an innovative entrepreneurial training program funded and supported by the National Science Foundation.
Through training, mentorship and competitive customer discovery funding, I-Corps supports teams in exploring customer needs, developing business models and commercializing their research.
Regional I-Corps training is perfect for early-stage, innovative ideas when you’re still exploring the market.
This role is often filled by a faculty member or the inventor of the technology.

Regional I-Corps training focuses on early-stage development and customer discovery, while the National I-Corps Teams program is aimed at scaling and commercialization, with specific eligibility requirements.
Your idea should be university-affiliated intellectual property that is innovative, scalable and fits within the realm of deep tech.
What Is “deep tech”?
“Deep tech” refers to groundbreaking scientific innovations and technologies that tackle complex challenges and have the potential to create transformative impacts.
If you’ve received an NSF award in the last five years, you can participate in the National I-Corps Teams program without going through regional training first.

A New Entrepreneur’s Guide to This Game-Changing Program Rachel Erbe 2025-10-22T12:13:04-07:00 October 22, 2025 By Cristy Salanga, Patent Manager, and I-Corps Project Director, Northern Arizona University Making an impact in this world begins with having a great idea. The challenge lies in turning that idea into a solution that customers or clients actually want. That’s where the NSF I-Corps program steps in, helping innovators bridge the gap between research and commercialization. If you’re an academic researcher or an innovator curious about how to bring your ideas to market, this will introduce you to the NSF I-Corps program and show why it’s a game-changer for innovators across the U.S. What is NSF I-Corps? The National Science Foundation (NSF) Innovation Corps (I-Corps TM ) is a federally funded program designed to introduce academic researchers and new entrepreneurs to the
Since its start in 2011, the program provides training, mentorship, and funding to university teams working on innovative technologies.
To reduce the risks of entrepreneurial ventures and increase the chances of success for early-stage startups, particularly those stemming from academic research.
In the research setting, this often consists of: Technical Lead (TL): Often a faculty member or researcher leading the technical development.
Entrepreneurial Lead (EL): Someone passionate about exploring the commercial potential of the idea, often a graduate student or postdoc working with the faculty member or researcher.

NSF I-Corps offers a combination of training, mentorship, and possible customer discovery funding (if eligible), including: Customer Discovery Training: The cornerstone of I-Corps is talking to people.
Mentorship: Participants are guided by experienced entrepreneurial instructors through the commercialization process and help them navigate the challenges of entrepreneurship.
Builds Confidence and Connections: With mentorship from experienced instructors and a cohort of like-minded individuals, teams gain the support they need to pursue their idea with confidence.
